Grace / Ben — I reviewed Sarah's asks and drafted a targeted redline. High level:

- Invoice routing: Add a new Section 6.3 (Invoice remit-to) that allows Customer to designate up to two remit-to legal entities for distinct charge categories ("Platform Services" and "Professional Services"). Each remit-to entry must include legal name, VAT/Tax ID, remit email, and invoicing entity. Redwood reserves the right to issue separate invoices per remit entity and to tie payment obligations to the entity listed on a given invoice.

- VAT / Reverse-charge: Insert clause referencing EU reverse-charge where applicable: Redwood will not charge VAT when Customer provides a valid EU VAT ID and indicates reverse-charge on the order form; Customer will be responsible for any VAT/withholding if VAT ID is invalid. Redwood will include standard VAT evidence on invoices (customer VAT ID, place of supply, and reverse-charge statement).

- Minimum commitment proration: Appendix A (Commitment Schedule) contains an optional monthly proration table: committed units can be pro-rated across months during a ramp period; any unused monthly units do not carry forward unless expressly agreed. If Customer wants upfront prepayment, that remains a separate checkbox.

I attached the redline (short diff) and a clean Order Form version. Ben — confirm if AP needs a single invoice per PO or if they can accept two invoices referencing the same PO number (procurement indicated the PO references the EU entity only). If procurement insists on a single PO and we must split, the workaround is to invoice platform usage to EU entity and services to the global entity with cross-reference to the PO in both invoices. That will require accounting to accept dual-entity billing for this deal.
